answer: One workable design: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because copper only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, shale is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any harbor approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
